items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: the trombone player, Billy Burns... and in the meantime we played for King Farouk's wedding

ctx.x: This is January 29, 1979. 65 Second Avenue, Jacques Butler, third tape.

The reason why Chitterson has been spoken of so much, Chitterson was the smallest man in the band and oh, we used to have some type of conspiracy and I was his buddy, I thought. So every night we were going to having camel rides, going to Cairo and seeing all the sights, the pyramids, and everything, all these lovely things, and I became very, very much attached to the Egyptians. They made me feel as I was one of them and I was trying to speak the language and I was learning fast, and this Mr. Pastotis (phonetic)…

Billy Burns was a caucasian man, but Billy Burns had a pair of lips on him that looked like steak lips, and he didn't care nothing about what he looked like. He was sort of man, he knowed what he looked like. He didn't want to hear it, he wanted to be a black man. / So, we left Billy Burns alone. Billy Burns had some rich woman, I think she was something -- the fiancee of the Minister of Finance of Belgium and Billy Burns would give parties and you would go in -- the bathtub would be full of Channel's Crepe de…
